senses.gloss:
अथ अ + थ (probably for अथा, Ved. cf. इदम्), adv.
 1. Then, Nal. 17, 35.
 2. Now, at the beginning of works and parts of works.
 3. But, Nal. 22, 13.
 4. In conditional sentences: If, अथ तान् नानु गच्छामि गमिष्यामि यमक्षयम्, ‘if I do not follow them, I shall go to the house of death,’ Rām. 2, 60, 3.
 --With following उ, (अथो): 1. [] afterwards, then, Chr. 56, 11. 2. and, Man. 2, 430. 3. even, Chr. 3, 1; and 23, 28.
 --With following अपि, nevertheless, Rām. 2, 29, 7.
 --With following वा: 1. or also, or, Man. 2, 219. Pañc. i, d. 399, वाथ instead of वाथ वा (cf. Pañc. iii, d. 36. अथो वा, Man. 3, 202). 2. or even, Bhartṛ. 2, 10. 3. but no, Śāk. 60, 18. 4. it is particularly used to introduce sentences: for, Pañc. 26, 14.
 --With following किम्: yes, well (in dialogue, cf. τί μήν).
 --Cf. Lat. at.

अथर्वन् अथर्वन् (borrowed from the Zend. आथ्र-वन्, derived from आतर्, ‘fire’), m.
 1. A priest.
 2. The name of a Ṛṣi, or saint.
 3. The Atharvaveda.

अथर्वाङ्गिरस अथर्वाङ्गिरस, i. e. अथर्वन्-अङ्गिरस् + अ.
 1. adj., f. सी. Revealed to Atharvan and Angiras, Man. 11, 33.
 2. sing and pl. The hymns of the Atharvaveda.
अथर्वी अथर्वी, f. (probably from अथर्वन्), The wife of a priest(?), Chr. 296, 10 = Rigv. 1, 112, 10.
आथर्वण आथर्वण, i. e. अथर्वन् + अ, adj., f. णी, Belonging to the Atharvaveda, Daśak. in Chr. 201, 11.
